Question B-003-015-011.

Why the correct answer is right: Too much sound-card audio overdrives the transmitter, producing splatter or energy outside the intended channel.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "Splatter or out-of-channel emissions": This is the correct choice because too much sound-card audio overdrives the transmitter, producing splatter or energy outside the intended channel.
- sourceIndex 1: "Higher signal-to-noise ratio": This is a near-miss because it shifts attention from Splatter or out-of-channel emissions. In digital information, packet forwarding, weak-signal modes, and sound-card drive level, more of that quantity would not address the fault and can make a clean-signal problem worse.
- sourceIndex 2: "Lower error rate": This answer would fit a different fault than Splatter or out-of-channel emissions. In digital information, packet forwarding, weak-signal modes, and sound-card drive level, reducing that quantity is not the mechanism that produces the correct effect here.
- sourceIndex 3: "Power amplifier overheating": This option confuses another station topic with Splatter or out-of-channel emissions. In digital information, packet forwarding, weak-signal modes, and sound-card drive level, power alone is not the control or safety mechanism being tested in this item.
